Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. Hayley Matthews and Qiana Joseph are at the crease for the West Indies Women. Renuka Singh Thakur has the ball in hand for India Women. Here we go.
…THE RUN CHASE…

West Indies Women were much better with the ball but dropped plenty of catches in the outfield. Deandra Dottin, Chinelle Henry, Hayley Matthews, and Afy Fletcher got a couple of wickets each while Karishma Ramharack bowled a tidy spell. The West Indies Women needs 160 to level the series. Can they do it or India Women defend this score and make it 2-0? We shall find out. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

India Women have managed to put a reasonable score on the board. After being asked to bat first, India Women were reeling at 48/3 but a fifty-run stand between Smriti Mandhana and Deepti Sharma got them back in the groove. Mandhana was dismissed for 62 while a handy cameo from Richa Ghosh down the order took the total past the 150-run mark.
Pitched full, outside leg. Renuka Singh Thakur swings and misses. A dot to end the innings. India Women finish on 159/9 from their 20 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness now as the teams and the umpires make their way out to the ground. Uma Chetry and Smriti Mandhana stride out to open the batting for India Women. It will be Chinelle Henry to start with the ball for the West Indies Women. We are moments away from the live action.

Pitch Report -  WV Raman is at the pitchside. He says that there is a little bit of grass on the surface. Adds that it is a good enough wicket for batting and doesn't think that the batters will face any problems. Shares that a bit of grass has been shaved off in the afternoon and the ends by adding that dew factor will come into play later in the evening.

Smriti Mandhana, the stand-in skipper for India Women says that they were looking to bowl first as well because of the dew factor. Adds that they will try to put a good score with the bat and defend it later like the previous game. Ends by sharing that Harmanpreet Kaur misses out with a niggle and Raghvi Bist will make her debut.

Hayley Matthews, the West Indies Women skipper has won the toss and opts to Bowl. She says that the conditions will suit to bat second and adds that they want to improve on certain aspects from the last game. Mentions that they made some strong plans but failed to execute. Ends by adding that that they made two changes with Ashwini Munisar and Nerissa Crafton coming in for Mandy Mangru and Shamilia Connell.

West Indies Women (Playing XI) - Hayley Matthews(C), Qiana Joseph, Shemaine Campbelle(WK), Deandra Dottin, Chinelle Henry, Nerissa Crafton (in place of Mandy Mangru), Shabika Gajnabi, Zaida James, Afy Fletcher, Karishma Ramharack, Ashmini Munisar (in place of Shamilia Connell).

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana(C), Uma Chetry, Jemimah Rodrigues, Raghvi Bist (in place of Harmanpreet Kaur), Richa Ghosh(WK), Sajana S, Deepti Sharma, Radha Yadav, Saima Thakor, Titas Sadhu, Renuka Singh Thakur.
Toss Update - West Indies Women have won the toss and opted to BOWL.

On the other hand, West Indies Women were below par in all three departments. Bowling first, they gave away close to 200 runs with only Karishma Ramharack doing a fine job with the ball. Chasing the score, West Indies Women lost early wickets but Qiana Joseph and Deandra Dottin kept them in the game till the halfway mark of the chase but the wicket of Dottin titled the game towards the home side as the Women in Maroon went down in the series opener. They are a quality side and will look to make a strong comeback and level the series. So, who are you backing to come out on top in this encounter? We shall find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit. Stay tuned!

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the second T20I in the three-match series between India Women and the West Indies Women from the Dr. DY Patil University Sports Ground in Navi Mumbai. After starting the series on a positive note, India Women will be riding high on confidence to seal the series while the West Indies Women will look to bounce back. In game one of the series, India Women batted first and posted a sizeable score of 195/4 with fifties from Smriti Mandhana and Jemimah Rodrigues and cameos from Uma Chetry and Richa Ghosh. With the ball, Titas Sadhu, Deepti Sharma, and Radha Yadav did a fine job to keep the West Indies Women to 146/7, winning by 49 runs. India Women will look to replicate their performance and make it 2-0 with a game in hand.
...MATCH DAY...

Two powerhouses in Women's cricket and especially in the T20 format, go head-to-head yet again in the 2nd T20I at the D.Y. Patil Sports Ground in Navi Mumbai. Yes, it is India Women taking on West Indies Women in the second game of the three-match T20I series with hosts India having already notched up a huge win in the first game. Hours before the first game on Sunday, 15 December, the WPL auction took place and veteran Deandra Dottin sealed a huge paycheck after missing out on the first two seasons and that only galvanized her more as she struck a wonderful fifty in the first game, albeit in a losing contest. India Women had an underwhelming Women's T20 World Cup, to say the least not too long ago but a few of their players are coming off some great experience in the WBBL and probably at the moment, no one in women's cricket is more in-form than Jemimah Rodrigues. She had a wonderful season with the Brisbane Heat Women, reaching the WBBL final and now in the first game she went on to make 73 runs off just 35 balls as India almost broke the 200-run barrier. Smriti Mandhana also seems to have got her mojo back as she too made a half-century and the Windies bowlers didn't have much answers on a pristine batting deck. However, West Indies Women will be wary about the fact that the squad they have right now, they do not bat deep and a lot depends on skipper Hayley Matthews and a couple of others and it showed as Titas Sadhu ran riot with her three-wicket haul. Fiery opener Qiana Joseph and the feisty competitor Deandra Dottin did show their brilliance but the lack of depth with the bat when they do concede so many runs is very tough to compete with. They need to make amends with the ball as that is their strength and be flawless in the field if they are to get back on level terms. A lot depends on Matthews, who didn't have her best game by any means last time around but if she gets going, it can be a real challenge for the Indians. Can West Indies Women come roaring back and level the series? Or will Harmanpreet Kaur and co. seal the series with a game in hand? We shall find out in due time.
